cues.text: Before changing trains in Germany, a passenger who cannot use stairs practises at home how to ask for the lift.
The existing station lesson explains platform two. It never teaches the lift question.
A trainer is preparing the lesson for this learner, who does not know the German words.
This learner cannot use stairs and does not know how to ask for the lift in German. Add that practice to the video, then preview it.
ChatGPT can translate the sentence. WebMCP adds the missing practice turn to this open video.
ChatGPT reads the open lesson, adds the lift practice, and opens its preview through the page's tools.
OpenScene supplies the approved words, filmed answer, route board, and timing.
The draft links the learner's need, German line, and pause.
During preview, the lesson stops before the answer and waits for the learner.
The learner selects the matching German line on the page.
Only then does the approved filmed response start, with the LIFT TO PLATFORM 2 board.
The learner can rehearse the exact exchange before the trip.
The trainer keeps the path. Undo remains, and every edit has a visible revision.
The page registers six narrow WebMCP tools. Filmed answers and timing stay page-approved.
This fictional lesson is for practice at home. It gives no live travel guidance.
